outcome.answer:
Automatically judging reports that help readers evaluate whether news is trustworthy can be done by generating reader-oriented, well-attributed trustworthiness reports and then using an automated judge to score the submissions against human-created rubrics. In the TREC 2025 DRAGUN Track, Task 2 produces a grounded report with citations, and the track’s AutoJudge process automatically judges new runs by comparing them to human importance-weighted rubrics derived from critical questions assessors expect readers to answer for trustworthiness assessment [1].

A related approach is to build an end-to-end system that generates critical questions, retrieves relevant evidence, and synthesizes concise trustworthiness reports with citations. One DRAGUN submission (UR_Trecking) combines LLM question generation with retrieval from a news corpus, evidence re-ranking and filtering, and LLM synthesis into trustworthiness reports grounded in selected evidence [2].

These differ mainly in scope: [1] emphasizes reusable automated evaluation (AutoJudge) against question-based trust rubrics, while [2] focuses on producing the trustworthiness reports themselves (with LLM-IR retrieval and synthesis).
